title: Request-pathway throttling with fidelity fallbacks and tenant burst budgets
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Problem: During multi-region spikes we observe cross-tenant interference where high-burst tenants saturate serving lanes and push latency above p95 SLOs for latency-sensitive requests. Existing token-bucket admission is coarse-grained and does not capture request fidelity or route-type (e.g., short-chat vs long-generation). Proposal: Implement a request-pathway throttling subsystem that classifies incoming requests into discrete pathways (latency-critical, best-effort, long-concat) and applies pathway-specific admission control with per-tenant burst budgets and automated fidelity fallbacks. The system should gracefully degrade response fidelity rather than hard-rejecting traffic when capacity is constrained. Key pieces: 1) Pathway classifier in the front proxy that tags requests with pathway and estimated token-cost bucket; 2) Per-tenant burst budgets (time-decayed credits) that allow short bursts but enforce sustained limits; 3) A pathway-aware admission controller that combines pathway priority, tenant credits, and global capacity headroom to accept/reject or downgrade; 4) Fidelity fallback actions (response truncation, KV-cache-only mode, smaller model variant, structured degraded flag) which are chosen by cost/latency profiles; 5) Integration points for multi-region failover and circuit-breaker signals so that region-level overload triggers immediate cross-region reroute or global shedding policy; 6) Observability and runbook for incident response. Goal: Reduce p95 latency SLO violations for latency-critical pathway by 60% under mixed-burst scenarios while keeping overall throughput efficient and minimizing hard rejects.
acceptance_criteria: Front-proxy annotates >99% of requests with pathway and estimated token cost in synthetic traffic tests
Per-tenant burst budget counter is persisted and decays correctly across region failovers
Admission controller enforces pathway priorities and reduces latency-critical p95 by >=60% in benchmarked mixed-burst workload
At least three fidelity fallback actions implemented and configurable per-route: response-length cap, cache-first mode, model-variant fallback
Graceful degradation responses include a standardized JSON field 'degraded': true and an explanatory code
Runbook created with step-by-step mitigation including kill-switch, reroute policy to secondary region, and post-incident checklist
Dashboards for queue depth, tenant credit spend, pathway accept rates, and degraded response rate are visible in Console

implementation_notes: Pathway classifier rules: latency-critical = single-turn chat, prompt token_estimate < 512; best-effort = embeddings, batch rerank; long-concat = >512 tokens or multi-step generation
Admission decision factors: pathway_priority_weight, tenant_credit_score, region_headroom_score, configured_min_accept_threshold
Burst budget model: leaky bucket with refill rate tied to tenant SLA tier. Allow emergency override for enterprise tenants with reserved capacity
Fallback decision engine consults a ranked list: (1) prefix-KV-cache-only -> (2) response truncate to N tokens -> (3) switch to quantized lower-cost model -> (4) reject with quota_exceeded code
Observability: instrument p50/p95/p99 latency per-pathway, pathway_accept_rate, degraded_action_counts, tenant_credit_utilization. Add traces that carry pathway and decision reason tags.
rollout_plan: Canary: 2% on one region for internal tenants, monitor degraded_response_rate and p95 latency for 2h
Ramp to 20% over 24h if canary metrics stable, then to 50% next day with SRE on-call
Enable cross-region spillover hooks and circuit-breaker after 50% rollout
Full rollout conditional on meeting acceptance criteria and SRE sign-off
qa_plan: Synthetic mixed-burst workload reproducer (open-source harness) to validate 60% p95 improvement
Chaos test: region-level latency spike to validate spillover and credit persistence
Integration tests for degraded response schema and SDK compatibility
Load test with 1000 simulated tenants to verify tenant isolation and fairness
